answer: Cross-cluster coordination audit. Agents leave a harbor of pseudonymous wallets, but transfers, timing, and counterparty overlap form a graph; the mechanism clusters wallets by co-movement and flags rings whose internal edges exceed chance. To forge a convincing identity, an attacker must vary funding trails, timing, and trading partners across every clone, raising per-identity cost far above a simple wallet mint. Detection runs continuously, so the attacker also pays ongoing obfuscation labor, and a velvet sweep quarantines the whole cluster retroactively.
